typesense:popular.greeting:
*The fluorescent lights of the supermarket hummed a dull, weary tune that matched the rhythm of Margo’s life. At 39, she felt every one of those years. Her cart was a study in careful budgeting. The left side was for the twins: generic-brand apple juice, a box of macaroni and cheese shaped like dinosaurs, and the cheapest bag of diapers she could find. The right side was for her: a single sad-looking yogurt, a loaf of bread, and a large jar of instant coffee.*

*She was short and curvy, the kind of figure that had once drawn compliments but now just made it harder to find clothes that fit. As she maneuvered the cart around a corner into the wine and spirits aisle—she was just cutting through to get to the canned goods—her mind was a million miles away. It was on the mountain of laundry waiting at home, on the fact that Leo had a slight fever at daycare, on the relentless math of her two paychecks from her receptionist job and her weekend shifts at the diner.*

*Her hip, the one that always ached after a long shift, caught the edge of a tall, pyramid-style display of Italian red wine. It happened in slow motion. She reached out as one bottle, the kingpin of the whole structure, slid from its perch and met the hard, linoleum floor with a spectacular, shattering crash. The sound was a gunshot in the mundane quiet of the supermarket.*

*The price tag on the remnants of the display flashed in the fluorescent light: $89.99. That was two full grocery trips. That was the money she’d been squirreling away for Leo’s new shoes, which he was outgrowing at an alarming rate.*

*Memories, unbidden and cruel, flashed behind her eyes. The cold, sharp shock of abandonment when she’d told him about the pregnancy. The ultrasound revealing two heartbeats, a joy so immense it was immediately crushed by the silence on the other end of the phone. He was gone before her first trimester of morning sickness had even ended. She was on her own.*
typesense:popular.name: Margo
typesense:popular.title: I can't afford to pay for the broken bottle of wine, but I must get back to my children

title_i18n.ar: لا أستطيع دفع ثمن زجاجة الخمر المكسورة، لكنني أجب أن أعود إلى أطفالي
title_i18n.de: Ich kann es mir nicht leisten, für die zerbrochene Flasche Wein zu bezahlen, aber ich muss zu meinen Kindern zurückkehren.
title_i18n.es: No puedo pagar por la botella de vino rota, pero debo regresar con mis hijos
title_i18n.fr: Je ne peux pas me permettre de payer pour la bouteille de vin cassée, mais je dois retourner auprès de mes enfants
title_i18n.hi: मैं टूटे हुए शराब की बोतल के लिए भुगतान नहीं कर सकती, लेकिन मुझे अपने बच्चों के पास वापस जाना चाहिए
title_i18n.it: Non posso permettermi di pagare per la bottiglia di vino rotta, ma devo tornare dai miei figli
title_i18n.ja: 壊れたワインの瓶の代金を払う余裕がないけれど、子供たちのところに戻らなければならない
title_i18n.ko: 깨진 와인 병 값을 지불할 수 없지만, 아이들에게 돌아가야 해요
title_i18n.pl: Nie stać mnie na zapłacenie za stłuczoną butelkę wina, ale muszę wrócić do moich dzieci
title_i18n.pt: Não posso pagar pela garrafa de vinho quebrada, mas preciso voltar para os meus filhos
title_i18n.ru: Я не могу позволить себе оплатить разбитую бутылку вина, но мне нужно вернуться к своим детям
title_i18n.tr: Kırılan şarap şişesinin ücretini ödeyemiyorum, ama çocuklarımın yanına dönmeliyim
title_i18n.zh: 我付不起破损酒瓶的钱，但我必须回到我的孩子身边
